newsitem.title: USA: Miami recovery-plan due date pushed to March.
newsitem.headline: Miami recovery-plan due date pushed to March.

text.p: Florida financial overseers pushed back to March a January 3 deadline for a five-year fiscal recovery plan they are demanding from the City of Miami, local newspapers said on Wednesday.

But the state oversight board put in place by Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles to ensure the city government's financial recovery kept the January 3 deadline for a new budget for the current fiscal year, the Miami Herald and Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel said.

The oversight board also eased back on a demand that all of this fiscal year's expenditures be covered by on-going revenues and will allow the city to obtain as much as 40 percent of its 1996-97 revenues from property sales and grants, the newspapers said.
Miami, a city of about 350,000 people, faces a $68 million budget gap in the fiscal year ending September 30.
The state oversight board had been insisting the city produce by January 3 a five-year balanced budget relying on so-call permanent fixes for its financial shortcomings.

In other steps taken Tuesday, according to the Sun-Sentinel, the board: agreed to hire an independent financial consultant; agreed than an independent trustee make all Miami's debt payments; and start reviewing all new city spending.
The board is scheduled to meet again on January 6.
